places.name: Alki Point
places.description: Landing site of the Denny Party in 1851, the founding settlement of what would become Seattle. Located on the western shore of Elliott Bay.

places.name: Duwamish River
places.description: River flowing into Elliott Bay, central to Duwamish tribal life and later industrialized as part of Seattle's harbor development.

places.name: Pioneer Square
places.description: Seattle's oldest neighborhood, devastated by the Great Fire of 1889 and rebuilt in brick and stone. The heart of early Seattle.

places.name: Pike Place Market
places.description: Seattle's iconic public farmers market, opened in 1907 to connect consumers directly with farmers. One of the oldest continuously operated public markets in the U.S.

places.name: Harbor Island
places.description: Artificial island at the mouth of the Duwamish River, created in the early 1900s and developed into a major shipbuilding and industrial center.

places.name: Boeing Plant 2
places.description: Boeing's massive wartime factory along the Duwamish River where B-17 and B-29 bombers were produced during World War II.

places.name: Colman Dock
places.description: Seattle's primary waterfront ferry terminal, built by James Colman in 1882. Served as the hub for Puget Sound ferry service for over a century.

places.name: Seattle Center
places.description: 74-acre civic campus built for the 1962 Century 21 Exposition (Seattle World's Fair). Home to the Space Needle, museums, and performance venues.

places.name: Space Needle
places.description: 605-foot observation tower built for the 1962 World's Fair, Seattle's most iconic architectural landmark.

places.name: Bellevue
places.description: City east of Seattle across Lake Washington. Became a major technology hub after Microsoft moved there in 1979.

places.name: Redmond
places.description: City east of Bellevue that became Microsoft's permanent headquarters location, transforming from a rural community to a tech center.

places.name: Medicine Creek
places.description: Creek near present-day Olympia where the 1854 Treaty of Medicine Creek was signed, ceding tribal lands including Vashon Island to the U.S. government.

places.name: Point Defiance Park
places.description: 760-acre park at the northern tip of Tacoma overlooking Puget Sound and Vashon Island, established in 1888. Site of the Tahlequah ferry terminal.

places.name: Ruston
places.description: Small city adjacent to Tacoma, site of the ASARCO copper smelter that operated from 1889 to 1985. Smelter emissions affected Vashon Island for decades.

places.name: Stadium High School
places.description: Tacoma landmark originally built as a luxury hotel in 1891, converted to a high school in 1906 after a fire. Notable for its French chateau-style architecture.

places.name: Tacoma Narrows
places.description: Strait connecting the main basin of Puget Sound with its southern reaches, between Tacoma and the Kitsap Peninsula. Site of the famous bridge collapse of 1940.

places.name: Puyallup
places.description: City southeast of Tacoma, home to the Puyallup Tribe and site of the Western Washington Fairgrounds used as Camp Harmony internment assembly center in 1942.

places.name: Puyallup Fairgrounds
places.description: Western Washington Fairgrounds in Puyallup, used as 'Camp Harmony' temporary assembly center where Japanese Americans were detained in 1942 before transfer to permanent internment camps.

places.name: Tacoma Dome
places.description: Large wooden-domed arena in Tacoma, opened in 1983. One of the largest wood-domed structures in the world.
